versions.label: Wofo M1
versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: Do you have time to do me a favor?
Woman: I'm about to run to the post office, but I can help you after that.
Man: I'm hosting this dinner party tonight, and I need to pick up some last-minute groceries.
Woman: What do you still need?
Man: I need vegetables and ingredients for a dessert. Here's a list.
Woman: No problem. I can swing by the market after I've mailed my package.
Man: You're a lifesaver. Thanks a million.

女：我正要去邮局，之后可以帮你。
男：今晚我办晚餐派对，还得临时买点食材。
女：还缺什么？
男：要蔬菜和做甜点的材料。这是清单。
女：没问题。寄完包裹我顺路去市场。
男：你真是救星。万分感谢。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: Hi, I need to return this sweater. I bought it yesterday, but it's too small for me.
Woman: Sure. Do you have the receipt?
Man: Yes, I have it right here.
Woman: Great. We can process the return. Do you want to exchange it for a larger size or get a refund?
Man: I'd like to exchange it, please.
Woman: No problem. I'll get another in that color for you from our stock.
Man: Thank you.

男：请帮我换货。
女：没问题。我从库存给您拿同色另一件。
男：谢谢。

versions.label: Wofo M1
versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: This is Jimmy Clerken from Rise Bakery calling. I received a message that you'd like to do a story about my shop for your university newspaper.
Woman: Yes, you've been a staple in our city for generations. The grandparents of our current students were customers there when they were young.
Man: It's a family-owned business, and we're proud of it. Would you be able to come next Monday at 3 o'clock?
Woman: Definitely. Is it all right if my photographer comes along?
Man: Of course. You can get different shots, even back in our kitchen where we do all the baking.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段对话。
男：我是 Rise Bakery 的 Jimmy Clerken。收到留言说你们校报想给我的店做一篇报道。
女：是的，你们在这座城市好几代人都是招牌。现在学生的祖父母小时候就在你们那儿买东西。
男：这是家族企业，我们很自豪。你们下周一 3 点能来吗？
女：当然。摄影师一起可以吗？
男：当然。可以拍不同角度，甚至到后面烘焙的厨房。

Man: I was just typing my paper and my computer suddenly shut down.
Woman: You've had a lot of problems with that laptop, haven't you? Have you tried holding down the power button for a few seconds?

Woman: How about you get in touch with my ex-roommate, Monica? She's a real tech whiz.
Man: That's an idea. Could you give me her number?
Woman: I'm not sure I have it anymore.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: Are Alyssa and David back from studying abroad in Hong Kong?
Woman: They returned last week. Alyssa is still adjusting to the time difference.
Man: I can relate. I had bad jet lag last summer after traveling across the globe. I kept taking long naps, which affected my sleep at night.
Woman: Instead of napping, getting outside for a walk and sunlight helps reset your internal clock. I told Alyssa the same.
Man: Once she's over it, let's all have lunch.
Woman: Sounds good. She just needs to sort out credit for an extra course she took over there. Then she'll be free.

versions.transcript:

Man: I just heard that the art store in the mall is going out of business.
Woman: Oh, no. I get painting supplies for my senior art project there.
Man: I know. That's why I came looking for you. What will you do now?
Woman: Well, I have a couple of options. I could get them online, or I can go to the store in Porterville, 10 miles away.
Man: Seems to me like you'd want to buy that kind of stuff in person.
Woman: I would. It looks like I'll be making regular trips to Porterville.

女：嗯，还有几个办法。可以网购，或者去十英里外 Porterville 那家店。
男：我觉得这类东西你应该想当面挑。
女：是啊。看来我得经常往 Porterville 跑了。

Woman: I was training a new employee yesterday, and I noticed that several pieces of info in the documents we use don't reflect our current practices here in the computer lab. Would you be able to help me update everything and print new copies?

Man: Our lease is up next month. Do we renew it or look for a new place? The landlord has raised our rent twice in two years. I think we should consider looking for a new place.

Narrator: Listen to a conversation.
Man: Have you booked the tickets for the sculpture garden yet?

Man: That's a good idea. In fact, they offer free entry on the first Saturday of the month.
Woman: Perfect. That's next weekend. Should we plan to go then?

Woman: Good idea. I'll send a message to everybody right now.

versions.label: Wofo M15
versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: Nice to meet you. I'm president of the student council at Galicia University. We're looking to book a place for our annual banquet, and you came highly recommended.
Woman: Great. When are you looking to have it? And about how many people do you expect — before the semester ends?
Man: Sometime in early May, and probably 50 to 60 people.
Woman: We have a private room upstairs. We can do a buffet-style meal, and we'll provide you with a projector, speakers, and anything else you may need.
Man: Sounds good. Now let's discuss the price.

请听一段对话。

女：好。打算什么时候办？大概多少人——学期结束前？
男：五月初左右，大概五十到六十人。
女：楼上有包间。可以做自助餐，还提供投影仪、音响和你们可能需要的其他东西。
男：听着不错。现在谈价钱吧。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: Hi Dr. Chin. I know you usually don't have office hours on Fridays, so thanks for your flexibility. I know how hectic things can get, especially at the end of the semester. So, I'm interested in writing my paper about Piaget and the stages of child development, but I just wanted to make sure that topic would be okay.
Woman: Well, it's pretty broad. It's only a five-page paper, so I'd pick one stage instead of trying to cover all of them. That way, you'll have time to get into details and really delve into the research.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: Hey Sarah, I heard that new gym opened near your house. Did you join it?
Woman: I did. It's impressive. State-of-the-art machines, a smoothie bar, and tons of classes. And best of all, it's within walking distance.

Man: Brave soul. I'd need a lot of coffee for that.
Woman: Ha, I probably would too.

男：哇，像度假水疗，还这么近。打算报什么课吗？
女：肯定要。本想试瑜伽课，但只在晚上，我那时要上班。也许改去早上 6 点的举重课，如果起得来的话。
男：真勇敢。我得靠大量咖啡。
女：哈，我大概也得。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: Have you tried that new Mediterranean restaurant on Maple Street?
Woman: I went there last night with my sister. The food was fantastic, especially the grilled fish. But there was a bit of a hiccup.
Man: Oh, what happened?
Woman: Well, we had a reservation for 7:00, but they didn't seat us until almost 7:45. Apparently, the kitchen was short-staffed and running behind.
Man: That is frustrating. Did the staff handle it well?
Woman: They were apologetic and even offered us complimentary appetizers while we waited.
Man: Sounds like they made up for it. I've been meaning to check it out.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段对话。
男：你试过 Maple Street 那家新开的地中海餐厅吗？
女：昨晚跟妹妹去了。菜很棒，尤其是烤鱼。不过有点小插曲。
男：哦，怎么了？
女：我们订的 7 点，结果差不多 7 点 45 才入座。据说厨房人手不够，进度落后。
男：挺烦人的。店员处理得怎么样？
女：他们很抱歉，等的时候还送了开胃菜。
男：听着像是弥补了。我一直想去试试。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: I've been looking for a job on campus, but nothing's working out.
Woman: That sounds frustrating. But there are so many options. Have you considered the library or the student union?
Man: Yes, but they're not hiring. I even tried the tutoring center, but they want prior experience. I can't count the number of times I've helped my roommate with biology, but I guess that's not officially experience.
Woman: Maybe you could volunteer first to build that experience?
Man: In theory, that sounds great. But I need to make money now. I went to the bookstore yesterday and spent way more than I had expected.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段对话。
男：我一直在找校内工作，但都不成。
女：听着挺挫败。不过选择很多。图书馆或学生会考虑过吗？
男：考虑过，但他们不招人。辅导中心也试了，但要有先前经验。帮室友补生物的次数我都数不清了，可那大概不算正式经验。
女：也许先做志愿攒经验？
男：理论上不错。但我现在就得赚钱。昨天去书店花的比预期多太多了。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.

Man: The biology department budget for next semester has been cut due to the funding freeze. We'll have to make some adjustments.
Woman: Have you reviewed spending on office supplies? Sometimes little things like that can add up.
Man: Yeah, we're probably spending more than necessary on paper and printer ink.
Woman: We could always switch to digital documents. Department meeting minutes, new course requests, things like that. I even know of a low-cost app we could use to organize everything.

女：可以改成电子文档。系会纪要、新课申请之类。我还知道一个低价应用能用来整理全部。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: My mobile phone is a few years old, and I've heard that updating to the newest operating system software can really slow it down.
Woman: That'd be annoying. So why not just keep the current operating system?
Man: An app I use requires the new one.
Woman: I see. Well, if all else fails, a lot of stores are offering good deals on new phones right now for the holidays.
Man: You know, that's not a bad idea. I'll definitely look into it. Now that I've got a job at the campus bookstore, I think it's feasible.

男：我用的一个应用要求新系统。

男：嗯，这主意不坏。我肯定会了解一下。现在我在校园书店有工作，应该负担得起。

Man: I'm really struggling in my biology class. The material just doesn't make sense to me. I'm not sure what to do.
Woman: You know, my roommate is a biology major, and she's worked at the tutoring center for about a year.
Man: Really? That could be useful.
Woman: I can put you in touch with her. And what about your other classes this semester?
Man: I don't have any issues in the other ones. I really like my archaeology class. The professor is actually leading a program in Egypt this summer. If only I had some extra money lying around.

男：真的？那可能有用。
女：我可以帮你联系她。这学期别的课呢？
男：别的没问题。我很喜欢考古课。教授今年夏天其实要带一个埃及项目。要是我手头多点闲钱就好了。

Woman: Well, that is my area of expertise. Let's discuss.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: I heard you got an internship at an advertising agency in town for the summer. That's so exciting!
Woman: I know, I start the first week of June. I actually just found out I also got offered an internship at an agency in Detroit. The company has a good reputation, but I'd have to move to another city, find an apartment...
Man: I see. Well, I'm glad one of us is having luck with internships.
Woman: You still haven't heard back from the architecture firm?
Man: No, considering the semester's over in a couple weeks, I think I should make other plans.

男：明白。好在我们俩总算有一个实习走运。
女：建筑事务所那边还没回你吗？
男：没有，再过几周学期就结束了，我觉得该做别的打算了。

versions.label: Wofo M29
versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: Our efforts have paid off. We've received additional funding from the university as well as several grants to support our art program.
Woman: Wonderful. I know how hard you worked on this.
Man: Everyone in the department contributed. Anyway, at the staff meeting we have scheduled, we'll discuss how to allocate the funds. The grants offer specific purposes, so we don't have much flexibility there.
Woman: Did we get the one to update our computers and design software?
Man: Partially. So we'll need to upgrade in phases. We'll start with the hardware first, because without it, we can't run the software.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段对话。
男：我们的努力有回报了。学校给了额外经费，还有几笔资助支持我们的艺术项目。
女：太好了。我知道你为这事付出很多。
男：系里每个人都出了力。总之，在我们安排好的教职工会上，会讨论怎么分配资金。那些资助有明确用途，所以那边灵活度不大。
女：更新电脑和设计软件的那笔批了吗？
男：部分批了。所以我们得分阶段升级。先从硬件开始，因为没有硬件跑不了软件。

Woman: Matt, you're back. How was your semester in Spain?

Woman: It sounds like you had a great experience. I thought about studying abroad in England, but I'm graduating in the spring, so...

versions.transcript:

versions.label: Wofo M35
versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Man: I didn't know the library hosted board game nights.
Woman: It doesn't. It's hosting a playtest, sponsored by Silverton Studios, a board game developer.
Man: What's a playtest?
Woman: It's when designers try out newly developed games to see what works. They tweak the game based on playtest results before marketing it.
Man: And university students are good playtest subjects.
Woman: I think so. We're trained to be critical thinkers. We're likely to notice what's confusing about a game or its rules, and say so.
Man: But what's in it for us?
Woman: Silverton Studios gives each participant a gift card.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段对话。
男：我不知道图书馆办桌游之夜。
女：不是。是试玩测试，由桌游开发商 Silverton Studios 赞助。
男：什么是试玩测试？
女：设计师试用新开发的游戏看什么好用。上市前根据试玩结果改游戏。
男：那大学生是好的试玩对象。
女：我觉得是。我们受过批判性思维训练。容易发现游戏或规则哪里让人糊涂，并说出来。
男：但我们有什么好处？
女：Silverton Studios 给每位参与者礼品卡。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Woman: You just started working at the bookstore, right? How's that going?
Man: It's okay. I like how it's close to my apartment. I can ride my bike there. I've mostly been processing orders and stocking the shelves. I just wish there was more variety. I'm doing the same tasks over and over again.

Man: Yes, but... well, my sister is the one who got me this job. She is friends with the owner, and I would feel bad quitting after working there for such a short time.

Woman: There's a temporary exhibit I'd really like to see this weekend at the university art museum. The one about New York City throughout the 19th century.

Woman: Why the photographs?

versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Woman: My schoolwork is really stressing me out.
Man: Have you considered trying yoga? My sister's taking a yoga class and says it's great for stress.
Woman: I haven't, but it sounds like a good idea. Do you know where I might start? Have you done yoga yourself?
Man: I haven't, but I know there are lots of classes for beginners. You should really look into it. I've also been thinking about taking a vacation during spring break. When's the last time you went anywhere for fun?
Woman: Thanks, but I like the yoga idea better. Why don't you find out where your sister attends her class and let me know.

versions.label: Wofo M50
versions.transcript:
Listen to a conversation.
Woman: Did you start next week's chapter in the psychology textbook?
Man: Yes, seems the main point is to take fewer notes, or did I miss something?
Woman: Not just fewer notes, but better notes. The chapter says if you try writing down every word from a lecture, you're transcribing, not thinking.
Man: I don't remember how they reach that conclusion. I mean the details.
Woman: Me neither. I'm going to double-check how many test subjects were in the study.
Man: I'm more interested in their age range. I mean, they were looking at university students, right?
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段对话。

男：看了。主要观点似乎是少记笔记，还是我漏掉了什么？
女：不只是少记笔记，而是要记更好的笔记。这一章说，如果你试图记下讲座中的每一个词，你是在抄录，而不是思考。
男：我不记得他们是如何得出这个结论的。我是说具体细节。
女：我也不记得。我打算再确认一下研究中有多少名受试者。
男：我对他们的年龄范围更感兴趣。我的意思是，他们研究的是大学生，对吧？

versions.transcript:

Man: In that urban planning lecture, it seemed like the professor feels that so-called green buildings actually hurt the environment.
Woman: She did make the point that if you import materials from far away, the carbon emissions, the pollution created during transit, add up, and that's not environmentally friendly.
Man: I think she ran out of time before she completely explained that idea of trade-offs, though.
Woman: True. She did say that she'll focus more on the positive aspects of green buildings that she didn't get to today.

versions.transcript:

Man: Did you hear the news about the robots? The university is acquiring robots, little automated carts that can bring food to students all around campus.

Woman: Hmm, well, that's true. Hopefully this won't replace them.
